answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each participant must lock a bonded stake of scarce resources—such as specialized walnut-derived compute credits—before joining any multi-agent voyage of shared work. An attacker creating many fake identities must acquire and escrow matching ivory-level scarce assets for every identity, so the total cost grows linearly with the number of sybils; successful detection triggers automatic slashing of the bond, making large-scale fake-identity attacks economically prohibitive.
